# Welcome to the RIPLRT Institute Research Group Manual {.unnumbered}

This is the operating system of the **RIPLRT Institute** — a mentee-powered environmental immunology and respiratory health equity research group. We translate environmental exposures into equitable respiratory and immune health through exposure science, immune and biomarker discovery, computational forecasting, reproducible analytics, bilingual science communication, and inclusive mentoring.

If you are reading this because you recently joined us: **welcome.** This manual is the fastest way to understand who we are, how we work, what we expect of one another, and how we give credit. If you are a returning member, treat it as a living reference — return to it when you onboard a new teammate, start a project, plan a manuscript, or hit a question about process.

::: {.callout-note}
## What this manual is — and isn't
This is a **culture document, onboarding guide, project-management playbook, mentoring compact, reproducibility guide, authorship policy, and operating system** in one. It is not a legal contract and does not override Lynn University policy, IRB protocols, sponsor terms, or applicable law. Where institutional policy and this manual disagree, institutional policy governs. Where this manual is silent, ask.
:::

## Our central narrative: Community-to-Clinic-to-Cloud

Everything we do follows one arc. We **measure and interpret environmental signals in communities**, **link them to clinical, claims, biomarker, and repository-based outcomes**, and **convert them into equity-aware decision tools** for clinicians, agencies, students, and the communities themselves.

Our scientific through-line is:

> **Exposure Science → Immune Bioactivity → Computational Forecasting → Equity-Focused Translation → Inclusive Workforce Development**

## How to read this manual

- **New members:** Read Chapters 1–9 in your first two weeks, then complete the onboarding checklist in the `/forms` appendix. Sign the acknowledgment form within your first 7 days.
- **Project leads:** Pay special attention to Chapters 6, 10, 11, 12, and 14, and use the project pod charter template before kickoff.
- **Mentors and mentees:** Chapters 7 and 8 are your compact. Use the IDP and one-on-one templates each semester.
- **Everyone:** Chapters 11–13 (data governance, reproducibility, and responsible AI) apply to all of us, all the time.

## A note on tone

We are a serious research group **and** a humane mentoring environment. Those are not in tension. We use "we" language because the lab belongs to all of us — it is *our* research group, not only the PI's. We state expectations directly because clarity is a form of respect. And we assume good faith, because that is how trust is built and how science gets done.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Suggest a change
This manual improves because members improve it. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` for how to propose edits via GitHub issues or pull requests, or raise it in a weekly huddle. Every contributor is acknowledged in the changelog.
:::
